title: 1 Samuel Chapter 21 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Samuel chapter 21 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 21 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Samuel Chapter 21.

questions.question: Who was the priest that David came to at Nob?
options: Ahimelech
Eli
Samuel
Abiathar
questions.correctAnswer: Ahimelech
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:1 states that David came to Nob to Ahimelech the priest.

questions.question: What was Ahimelech's initial reaction when he saw David alone?
options: He was afraid
He was joyful
He was angry
He was confused
questions.correctAnswer: He was afraid
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:1 says Ahimelech was afraid at the meeting of David and asked why he was alone.

questions.question: Why did David say he was alone and no man was with him?
options: The king commanded secrecy about the business
He was on a secret mission from the priest
He was avoiding Saul's men
He was sick and could not bring others
questions.correctAnswer: The king commanded secrecy about the business
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:2 records David telling Ahimelech the king commanded him a business and no man should know about it.

questions.question: What did David request from Ahimelech?
options: Five loaves of bread or what was present
A sword and armor
Water and provisions
A horse and chariot
questions.correctAnswer: Five loaves of bread or what was present
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:3 shows David asking for five loaves of bread or what was at hand.

questions.question: What kind of bread did Ahimelech say he had under his hand?
options: Hallowed bread
Common bread
No bread at all
Freshly baked bread
questions.correctAnswer: Hallowed bread
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:4 states that there was no common bread, only hallowed bread.

questions.question: According to Ahimelech, what condition must the young men have kept to eat the hallowed bread?
options: They must have kept themselves from women
They must be priests
They must fast for a day
They must offer a sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: They must have kept themselves from women
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:4 says the bread is for young men who have kept themselves at least from women.

questions.question: True or False: David told the priest that the young men had been kept from women for about three days.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 21:5 David states women have been kept from them about three days.

questions.question: True or False: David said the bread was completely common and not sanctified at all.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:5 clarifies the bread was 'in a manner common, yea, though it were sanctified this day in the vessel,' so it was not completely common.

questions.question: What bread did the priest give David since there was no common bread?
options: Hallowed bread taken from before the LORD
Freshly baked bread
Barley bread
Unleavened bread
questions.correctAnswer: Hallowed bread taken from before the LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:6 says the priest gave hallowed bread taken from before the LORD (the shewbread).

questions.question: Who was the servant of Saul present that day at Nob?
options: Doeg the Edomite
Abner the captain
Joab the general
Jonathan the son of Saul
questions.correctAnswer: Doeg the Edomite
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:7 identifies Doeg, an Edomite and chief herdman of Saul, was present.

questions.question: True or False: David brought his sword and weapons with him when he came to Nob.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:8 records David saying he did not bring his sword or weapons because the king's business required haste.

questions.question: What notable sword did Ahimelech show David?
options: The sword of Goliath the Philistine
The sword of Saul
The sword of Jonathan
The sword of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: The sword of Goliath the Philistine
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:9 says the sword of Goliath, whom David slew, was wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod and offered to David.

questions.question: Where did David go after fleeing from Saul that day?
options: Gath
Jerusalem
Bethlehem
Hebron
questions.correctAnswer: Gath
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:10 states David fled and went to Achish the king of Gath.

questions.question: What did the servants of Achish say about David?
options: He was famous for killing tens of thousands
He was a thief
He was a mad man
He was a prophet
questions.correctAnswer: He was famous for killing tens of thousands
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:11 says the servants asked if this was David, who was praised for killing thousands and ten thousands.

questions.question: How did David behave before the servants of Achish?
options: Feigned himself mad
Sang a song
Told them the truth
Bowed respectfully
questions.correctAnswer: Feigned himself mad
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:13 states David feigned madness by scrabbling on doors and letting spittle fall on his beard.

medium.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 21 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Samuel Chapter 21 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What kind of bread did Ahimelech give David when he requested food?
options: Hallowed bread
Common bread
Barley bread
Unleavened bread
questions.correctAnswer: Hallowed bread
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:6 states that the priest gave David hallowed bread because there was no other bread present but the shewbread, which was holy.

questions.question: Who was Doeg, whom the text mentions as present when David met Ahimelech?
options: A servant of Saul and chief of his herdmen
A priest of Nob
A warrior from Gath
David's servant
questions.correctAnswer: A servant of Saul and chief of his herdmen
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:7 identifies Doeg as a servant of Saul and the chief of the herdmen belonging to Saul.

questions.question: Why did David not bring his sword or weapons with him when he came to Ahimelech?
options: Because the king's business required haste
Because he was disarmed by Saul
Because he trusted God to protect him
Because he wanted to appear peaceful
questions.correctAnswer: Because the king's business required haste
questions.explanation: According to 1 Samuel 21:8, David told Ahimelech he did not bring weapons because the king's business required haste.

questions.question: What weapon did Ahimelech offer David that had special significance?
options: The sword of Goliath the Philistine
A spear from Saul's armory
A bow and arrows
A dagger from Nob
questions.correctAnswer: The sword of Goliath the Philistine
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:9 explains that Ahimelech offered David the sword of Goliath, whom David had slain in the valley of Elah.

questions.question: What was David’s reaction to the offer of the sword of Goliath?
options: He accepted it, saying there was none like it
He declined, trusting in God’s protection
He asked for a different weapon
He took it but was hesitant
questions.correctAnswer: He accepted it, saying there was none like it
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:9 records David’s response that there was no sword like that, so he requested it.

questions.question: After receiving the bread and sword, where did David flee to and why?
options: To Achish king of Gath, fleeing from Saul
To Jerusalem, to seek refuge
To Nob, to hide among priests
To the wilderness, to pray
questions.correctAnswer: To Achish king of Gath, fleeing from Saul
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:10 states that David fled that day for fear of Saul and went to Achish king of Gath.

questions.question: How does David’s interaction with Ahimelech about the bread demonstrate practical faith in God?
options: He trusted God’s provision even when only holy bread was available
He demanded common bread despite the priest’s warning
He refused to eat the bread, relying solely on prayer
He took bread secretly without permission
questions.correctAnswer: He trusted God’s provision even when only holy bread was available
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 21:4-6, David accepts the hallowed bread, showing trust in God’s provision despite it being sacred and not common bread.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 21:9 teach us about God’s provision through human means in times of need?
options: God can provide uniquely through unexpected resources, like Goliath’s sword
God only provides through prayer, not physical weapons
God does not support use of weapons
God expects us to fight without any tools
questions.correctAnswer: God can provide uniquely through unexpected resources, like Goliath’s sword
questions.explanation: The sword of Goliath given to David (1 Samuel 21:9) symbolizes God’s provision through unusual means during urgent needs, affirming trust in divine provision.

questions.question: A believer struggles with fear when facing enemies. Based on 1 Samuel 21:10-13, what biblical truth can encourage them?
options: Sometimes feigning weakness or relying on God’s wisdom can protect you
Fighting fear requires immediate confrontation
Running away is always wrong
One must hide without any strategy
questions.correctAnswer: Sometimes feigning weakness or relying on God’s wisdom can protect you
questions.explanation: David’s feigned madness before Achish (1 Samuel 21:13) illustrates using God-given wisdom and strategy to overcome fear and danger.

questions.question: What lesson about integrity can be drawn from David’s explanation to Ahimelech regarding the sanctity of the bread and the purity of his men?
options: Being truthful about one’s circumstances honors God
It is acceptable to lie for convenience
One should avoid priests when in trouble
Purity is unimportant in times of need
questions.correctAnswer: Being truthful about one’s circumstances honors God
questions.explanation: David honestly explained the purity of his men and the condition of the bread to Ahimelech (1 Samuel 21:4-5), showing integrity even under pressure.

questions.question: According to the context of 1 Samuel 21, what does David’s reliance on the priest’s provision teach about humility and dependence?
options: Relying on others’ help shows humility and trust in God’s provision
Self-sufficiency is paramount
One should avoid asking for help
Dependence is a sign of weakness
questions.correctAnswer: Relying on others’ help shows humility and trust in God’s provision
questions.explanation: David’s approach to Ahimelech for bread and weapons (1 Samuel 21:1-9) shows humility and reliance on God’s provision through others.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 21:7-9 imply about the potential dangers of associating with those who serve worldly powers?
options: Such associations may expose God’s people to harm or betrayal
All servants of kings are trustworthy
Priests are always protected regardless of company
Serving kings guarantees safety
questions.correctAnswer: Such associations may expose God’s people to harm or betrayal
questions.explanation: Doeg, a servant of Saul present at Nob (1 Samuel 21:7), later becomes an instrument of betrayal, showing risks in these associations.

questions.question: True or False: David brought his sword with him when he went to see Ahimelech because he expected danger.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:8 explicitly says David did not bring his sword or weapons because the king’s business required haste.

questions.question: True or False: David’s behavior before King Achish was an example of using wisdom to protect his life.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 21:13, David feigned madness to protect himself, showing practical wisdom in a dangerous situation.

questions.question: True or False: The bread given to David was common bread that anyone could eat without restriction.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:4-6 clarifies the bread was hallowed bread, set aside before the LORD, not common bread.

hard.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 21 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Samuel Chapter 21.

questions.question: What was the reaction of Ahimelech the priest when David came to Nob alone?
options: He was afraid and questioned why David was alone
He welcomed David with joy and celebration
He immediately gave David food and weapons without question
He sent David away fearing Saul
questions.correctAnswer: He was afraid and questioned why David was alone
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:1 states that Ahimelech was afraid at the meeting of David and asked why he was alone without any men with him.

questions.question: Why did David say he was alone when he spoke to Ahimelech?
options: The king had commanded him on a secret business and sent his servants elsewhere
He was ashamed to bring his men
His men were all sick and could not come
He was scouting for enemies
questions.correctAnswer: The king had commanded him on a secret business and sent his servants elsewhere
questions.explanation: According to 1 Samuel 21:2, David told Ahimelech that the king had commanded him on a business and had told him to keep it secret, appointing his servants to another place.

questions.question: What kind of bread did Ahimelech offer David when David asked for bread?
options: Hallowed bread, the shewbread
Common bread from the market
Barley bread baked that morning
Unleavened bread for a festival
questions.correctAnswer: Hallowed bread, the shewbread
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:6 explains that the priest gave David the hallowed bread, specifically the shewbread, because there was no common bread available.

questions.question: Who was Doeg, mentioned in this chapter?
options: An Edomite servant of Saul and chief herdman
David's loyal warrior
A priest in Nob
King Achish's advisor
questions.correctAnswer: An Edomite servant of Saul and chief herdman
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:7 identifies Doeg as an Edomite, the chiefest of Saul's herdmen, who was present that day.

questions.question: What weapon did Ahimelech offer David when David asked if there was a sword or spear available?
options: The sword of Goliath wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod
A spear used in the king's army
A common sword used by priests
A bow and arrows
questions.correctAnswer: The sword of Goliath wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:9 states that Ahimelech gave David the sword of Goliath the Philistine, which was wrapped behind the ephod.

questions.question: What did David do when he fled to Achish, king of Gath?
options: He pretended to be mad to avoid harm
He openly declared himself a king
He brought his men to fight for Achish
He asked for sanctuary peacefully
questions.correctAnswer: He pretended to be mad to avoid harm
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:13 describes how David feigned madness before the servants of Achish by scrabbling on the doors and letting his spittle fall on his beard.

questions.question: What was Achish's reaction when he saw David's behavior?
options: He said David is mad and questioned why he was brought to him
He welcomed David as a noble guest
He prepared a feast in David's honor
He imprisoned David immediately
questions.correctAnswer: He said David is mad and questioned why he was brought to him
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:14 records Achish telling his servants that David appeared mad and asking why they had brought him before him.

questions.question: What does David's fear of Achish reveal about his situation at Gath?
options: David was afraid because he was in enemy territory and vulnerable
David was confident because Achish was his ally
David expected Achish to help him fight Saul
David planned to overthrow Achish
questions.correctAnswer: David was afraid because he was in enemy territory and vulnerable
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:12 explains that David laid the words of Achish’s servants in his heart and was sore afraid of the king of Gath, indicating his vulnerability in foreign territory.

questions.question: True or False: The bread given to David was common bread used every day by the people.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 21:4-6 clarifies that the bread given to David was hallowed bread, specifically the shewbread, which was consecrated and not common daily bread.

questions.question: True or False: David’s feigning madness before Achish is an example of a literary device called irony.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: David pretending to be mad to save himself is ironic because though he is sane and a mighty warrior, he acts mad to avoid danger, as seen in 1 Samuel 21:13. This irony contrasts expectation and reality.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of a righteous man feigning madness to escape danger, similar to David's behavior in 1 Samuel 21?
options: Jeremiah 29:26, where the prophet feigns madness before the Babylonians
Genesis 12:10, Abram's sojourn in Egypt
Exodus 14:13, Moses before the Red Sea
Daniel 1:8, Daniel refusing the king's food
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 29:26, where the prophet feigns madness before the Babylonians
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 29:26 mentions the prophet Jeremiah being accused of feigning madness in the presence of the Babylonians, similar to David's feigned madness before Achish in 1 Samuel 21:13.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Hebrew word 'shewbread' (showbread) given to David?
options: It was bread placed before the LORD as a continual offering and only priests could eat it
It was ordinary bread baked daily for common consumption
It was unleavened bread eaten only at Passover
It was bread used for making sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: It was bread placed before the LORD as a continual offering and only priests could eat it
questions.explanation: The 'shewbread' was holy bread placed on the table before the LORD in the tabernacle and was only to be eaten by priests, as in 1 Samuel 21:6, reflecting its sacred nature.

questions.question: How does David’s receiving the sword of Goliath symbolize a typological fulfillment in the biblical narrative?
options: It symbolizes David's continuing victory over enemies and God's empowerment
It represents David's submission to Saul's authority
It foreshadows David becoming a priest
It indicates David's retirement from battle
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes David's continuing victory over enemies and God's empowerment
questions.explanation: The sword of Goliath, which David took in 1 Samuel 21:9, symbolizes his previous victory and God's empowerment, typologically pointing to his future role as king and victorious leader.

questions.question: Which Old Testament theme is developed in this chapter through David’s flight and reliance on the sanctuary for provision and protection?
options: The theme of divine protection and refuge in times of distress
The theme of royal coronation rituals
The theme of covenant renewal
The theme of sacrificial atonement
questions.correctAnswer: The theme of divine protection and refuge in times of distress
questions.explanation: David’s visit to the priest and receiving of holy bread in 1 Samuel 21:1-6 shows reliance on God’s provision and sanctuary as refuge, reflecting the recurring biblical theme of divine protection.

questions.question: How does the historical context of Nob’s priesthood help explain Ahimelech’s fear when David arrives alone?
options: Because Nob was a priestly city allied with Saul, unusual solitary visits could signal danger
Because Nob was a Philistine city hostile to Israel
Because the priests were forbidden to meet with David
Because Ahimelech was afraid of Saul’s spies everywhere
questions.correctAnswer: Because Nob was a priestly city allied with Saul, unusual solitary visits could signal danger
questions.explanation: Nob was a city of priests loyal to Saul, so Ahimelech’s fear in 1 Samuel 21:1 reflects concern over David’s solitary visit potentially bringing danger from Saul’s enemies.

theological.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 21 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Samuel Chapter 21 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does David's request for bread from Ahimelech in 1 Samuel 21:3 reveal about God's provision for His servants?
options: God provides materially even in unusual circumstances
God expects His servants to fast regularly
God only provides for the king's direct family
God demands complete self-sufficiency from His followers
questions.correctAnswer: God provides materially even in unusual circumstances
questions.explanation: David's request for bread despite being on a secret mission shows God's provision through human agents even in extraordinary situations (1 Samuel 21:3). This illustrates God's ongoing care for His servants as affirmed in Psalm 37:25.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is demonstrated by Ahimelech's hesitation to give common bread, offering only holy bread to David and his men in 1 Samuel 21:4?
options: The sanctity required in approaching God
The exclusivity of the priesthood
The necessity of ritual sacrifice
The redundancy of the Mosaic Law
questions.correctAnswer: The sanctity required in approaching God
questions.explanation: Ahimelech's response shows the doctrine of holiness, emphasizing that the bread set aside was consecrated and not common, reflecting God's demand for sanctification among His people (1 Samuel 21:4). This aligns with Leviticus 11:44's call to be holy because God is holy.

questions.question: How does David's explanation in 1 Samuel 21:5 about the sanctity of his men illustrate the doctrine of sanctification?
options: Sanctification involves moral purity and separation
Sanctification is only for priests
Sanctification is unnecessary for God’s servants
Sanctification depends solely on ritual acts
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves moral purity and separation
questions.explanation: David's claim that his men have kept themselves from women and are holy indicates sanctification as moral and physical separation, a state required to partake of holy things (1 Samuel 21:5). This supports the biblical teaching in 1 Thessalonians 4:3-4 about sanctification.

questions.question: What does the presence of Doeg the Edomite in 1 Samuel 21:7 reveal about the human condition and sin’s pervasiveness?
options: Sin and betrayal can be found even among God's people
Only outsiders like Edomites are sinful
Sin is limited to kings and priests
God protects His servants from all betrayal
questions.correctAnswer: Sin and betrayal can be found even among God's people
questions.explanation: Doeg’s presence as a servant of Saul and an Edomite who would later betray Ahimelech shows that sin and treachery infiltrate even those associated with God’s people, demonstrating human fallenness (1 Samuel 21:7). This is consistent with Jeremiah 17:9 on the deceitfulness of the human heart.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted by the availability of Goliath’s sword to David as described in 1 Samuel 21:9?
options: God’s sovereign provision for victory
God’s wrath against enemies
God’s invisibility
God’s judgment only on kings
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereign provision for victory
questions.explanation: The sword of Goliath, a symbol of God’s past victory through David, being available shows God's sovereignty in providing means for His servant's protection and success (1 Samuel 21:9). This aligns with Exodus 14:14 where God fights on behalf of His people.

questions.question: How does David’s flight to Achish, king of Gath, in 1 Samuel 21:10 fit the broader redemptive narrative of Scripture?
options: It foreshadows the Messiah’s rejection and exile
It indicates the failure of the Davidic covenant
It shows the end of Israel’s monarchy
It confirms David’s unworthiness as king
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the Messiah’s rejection and exile
questions.explanation: David’s flight and fear typify the Messiah’s rejection and suffering in exile before ultimate kingship, fitting into the biblical theme of the suffering servant (1 Samuel 21:10). This is typologically connected with Psalm 22 and Isaiah 53.

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by the servants of Achish recognizing David’s fame in 1 Samuel 21:11?
options: God’s anointed are known beyond Israel
God limits His work to Israel alone
Human fame guarantees divine approval
The king’s popularity is based on military might
questions.correctAnswer: God’s anointed are known beyond Israel
questions.explanation: The servants’ recognition of David’s renown shows that God’s anointed king’s reputation extends beyond Israel, supporting the doctrine of God’s sovereignty over all nations (1 Samuel 21:11). This anticipates Psalm 72:8-11 where kings of all nations serve the Messiah.

questions.question: What does David’s fear of Achish in 1 Samuel 21:12 reveal about human frailty and reliance on God?
options: Even God’s chosen can experience fear and need divine help
Fear is a sign of weak faith
God abandons His servants in danger
Faith eliminates all human emotions
questions.correctAnswer: Even God’s chosen can experience fear and need divine help
questions.explanation: David’s fear illustrates that God’s servants are still human and vulnerable, emphasizing the need to trust God amid threats (1 Samuel 21:12). This accords with Psalm 56:3 where David expresses trust despite fear.

questions.question: How does David’s feigning madness before Achish in 1 Samuel 21:13 demonstrate a theological tension between human wisdom and divine providence?
options: Human wisdom sometimes complements divine providence in protection
God forbids any human cunning
Divine providence excludes human action
God punishes deception in all forms
questions.correctAnswer: Human wisdom sometimes complements divine providence in protection
questions.explanation: David’s act shows that human prudence and tactics can be used by God to fulfill His purposes, reflecting a synergy between human action and divine providence (1 Samuel 21:13). Proverbs 3:5-6 encourages reliance on God while using wisdom.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do 1 Samuel 21:4-6 and 1 Samuel 21:9 convey about holiness and God’s provision in times of distress?
options: God’s provision requires reverence and holiness but does not fail in urgent need
God’s provision is limited to priests only
Holiness is irrelevant in crises
God’s provision is always common and unrestricted
questions.correctAnswer: God’s provision requires reverence and holiness but does not fail in urgent need
questions.explanation: The passage teaches that while holiness (1 Samuel 21:4-6) governs access to God’s provision, God still provides in extraordinary ways during urgent needs, as David received holy bread and Goliath’s sword (1 Samuel 21:9). Hebrews 12:14 stresses holiness’s importance, while Philippians 4:19 affirms God’s provision.

questions.question: What synthesis of teaching about human fear and God’s sovereignty is found by comparing 1 Samuel 21:7 and 1 Samuel 21:12?
options: Human fear coexists with God’s sovereign control over circumstances
Fear means God is not in control
God removes all dangers instantly
Faith removes fear completely
questions.correctAnswer: Human fear coexists with God’s sovereign control over circumstances
questions.explanation: The presence of Doeg (1 Samuel 21:7) and David’s fear of Achish (1 Samuel 21:12) together show that while believers face threats, God remains sovereign over all situations, allowing fear but inviting trust (Isaiah 41:10).

questions.question: What does the interaction between David and Ahimelech in 1 Samuel 21:1-2 teach about divine-human interaction under secrecy and obedience?
options: Obedience to God’s commands sometimes requires secrecy and trust
God forbids secrecy in His plans
Human plans override divine commands
Obedience excludes any human communication
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God’s commands sometimes requires secrecy and trust
questions.explanation: David’s secret mission (1 Samuel 21:1-2) reveals that obedience to God’s purposes can involve confidentiality and trust in God’s guidance, reflecting the hidden workings of divine providence (Ecclesiastes 3:7).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that David’s deception in feigning madness (1 Samuel 21:13) contradicts biblical morality. What does 1 Samuel 21:10-15 actually teach about this behavior?
options: It shows that God can use human actions, even deception, to preserve His plans
It endorses lying as a general moral principle
It condemns David’s behavior as sinful
It suggests God is indifferent to human morality
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that God can use human actions, even deception, to preserve His plans
questions.explanation: David’s feigned madness in 1 Samuel 21:13 is a strategic act used by God to protect His anointed king, demonstrating divine sovereignty over human actions without endorsing deception as an ethical norm (Exodus 1:15-21 shows similar protective deception).

questions.question: What combined theological insight about divine holiness and human access to sacred things emerges from 1 Samuel 21:4-6 and 1 Samuel 21:8-9?
options: Holiness governs access to God’s provision, yet God equips His servants for their mission
Sacred things are only for priests and never for laypersons
God’s provision is random and unregulated
Physical weapons have no spiritual significance
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness governs access to God’s provision, yet God equips His servants for their mission
questions.explanation: The holy bread (1 Samuel 21:4-6) and Goliath’s sword (1 Samuel 21:8-9) show that while holiness is required for access to God’s provision, God equips His servants both spiritually and materially for their calling, consistent with Ephesians 6:10-17.

questions.question: How does David’s flight from Saul to Achish in 1 Samuel 21:10-12 contribute to the biblical narrative of the suffering king who will ultimately reign?
options: It typifies the Messiah’s suffering before triumph
It shows that kings are always victorious immediately
It denies the idea of a suffering servant
It suggests kingship is based on human power alone
questions.correctAnswer: It typifies the Messiah’s suffering before triumph
questions.explanation: David’s fear and exile prefigure the Messiah’s journey of suffering and rejection before establishing His kingdom, fitting the biblical theme in Isaiah 53 and Luke 24:26.
